sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *sin embargo* from A2 Unit 28 and *no obstante* from B1 Unit 1. Both join two facts that pull in different directions: something expected, and what happened instead. *No obstante* is a little more formal. Put a semicolon or a full stop before them and a comma after them. This is useful when you tell a hard story, because the connector shows the turn without any opinion from you.

sections.title: Two facts, one contrast
rows: Muchos esperaban un obispo tranquilo; sin embargo, Romero habló por las víctimas.
Many expected a quiet bishop; however, Romero spoke for the victims.
La guerra fue dura; no obstante, las dos partes llegaron a un acuerdo.
The war was hard; nevertheless, the two sides reached an agreement.
Hubo muchas amenazas. Sin embargo, Romero siguió hablando por la radio.
There were many threats. However, Romero kept speaking on the radio.
Había miedo; no obstante, mucha gente escuchaba la misa en casa.
There was fear; nevertheless, many people listened to Mass at home.

sections.title: In the story of El Salvador

items.spanish: La guerra duró doce años. Sin embargo, en 1992 se firmó la paz.
items.english: The war lasted twelve years. However, peace was signed in 1992.

items.spanish: La guerra fue muy violenta; no obstante, las dos partes negociaron con la ayuda de la ONU.
items.english: The war was very violent; nevertheless, the two sides negotiated with the help of the UN.

items.spanish: Romero fue nombrado arzobispo en 1977; sin embargo, pocas semanas después empezó a hablar con más fuerza.
items.english: Romero was named archbishop in 1977; however, a few weeks later he began to speak out more strongly.

items.spanish: Hubo amenazas; no obstante, la misa se oía por la radio cada domingo.
items.english: There were threats; nevertheless, the Mass was heard on the radio every Sunday.

sections.content: *Sin embargo* and *no obstante* do not mean *por eso* ("that is why"): after them the second fact goes against the first one. Do not put *que* after them.
